items.text: System MUST show signed-in members their own claims from the last 24 months by date of service, newest first, including ended coverage; adjusted claims appear once, as the latest version.
System MUST show each claim's number, date of service, provider, status, amount billed, plan paid and what the member may owe (once processed).
System MUST show claim information no more than 24 hours behind the claims system, with its "Updated" time, and say plainly when it can't refresh.
System MUST show a plain-language empty state when there are no claims.
System MUST give each claim one of the six statuses, using Claims Operations' mapping, with plain-language text on what happens next.
System MUST say whom a Waiting for information claim awaits (provider or member) and what, if anything, the member must do.
System MUST show every service line with a plain-language description, amounts and its own status, and say "Processed by your other plan first" when another plan paid first.
System MUST show for denials the plain-language reason, how and by when to appeal, a link to the existing appeal process, and the EOB.
System MUST show "We're reviewing this claim. Please contact us." for unmapped codes, never the code, and log the gap for Claims Operations.
System MUST NOT show diagnosis codes, clinical notes or other clinical detail.

System MUST let only the subscriber see dependents' claims, by age on the viewing day: under 13, all; 13–17, all but sensitive-service claims (per Contoso's privacy policy); 18 and over, none. It MUST show none for a dependent with a confidential communication request, or whose age or privacy status it can't confirm.
System MUST leave no trace of hidden claims in any list, count, total, message or EOB, and answer requests for them exactly as for nonexistent claims.
System MUST show one privacy note on every dependent's page and, for dependents 18 and over, that their claims are private, whether or not any exist.
System MUST offer an accessible EOB for Processed, Denied and Adjusted claims, explain other formats and languages, and say when one isn't ready (usually 3 business days after processing).
System MUST audit-log every view of claim information and every EOB request: who, whose claim, which claim, what and when.
System MUST show status labels, reason text and next steps in English or Spanish, per the member's language preference.
System MUST meet WCAG 2.2 AA on every member-facing page.
System MUST clear claim information from the screen on session timeout and return the member to the same page after sign-in.

member CHP-0004417 has recent claims | they open Claims | they see each claim's number, date of service, provider, status, amount billed, plan paid and what they may owe, newest first, with the "Updated" time.
a new member with no claims | they open Claims | they're told claims usually appear a few weeks after a visit.
the claims system is down and claims were updated 6 hours ago | the member opens Claims | those claims show with the "Updated" time and a note that recent changes may be missing.
claims haven't been updated for over 24 hours | the member opens Claims | no claims show, and a message explains how to get help.
an adjusted claim | the member opens Claims | it appears once, as its latest version, labeled Adjusted.
processed claim CLM-2026-000183 has three lines | the member opens it | each line shows a plain-language description and amounts, and no diagnosis codes or clinical notes appear.
claims waiting on the provider and on the member's other-insurance details | the member opens each | each says who we're waiting on and what, if anything, the member must do.
a denied claim | the member opens it | they see the plain-language reason, how to appeal and by when, and the EOB.
one of a claim's three lines was denied | the member opens it | each line shows its own status, and the denied line its reason.
a denial reason with no plain-language mapping | the member opens the claim | a generic "We're reviewing this claim" message replaces the code, and the gap is logged for Claims Operations.
the 9-year-old has claims, including CLM-2026-000201 | the subscriber opens them | all are shown, and each view is audit-logged.
the 16-year-old has two routine claims and one sensitive-service claim | the subscriber views that dependent | only the routine claims appear, and no count, total or message hints at a third.
the 19-year-old | the subscriber selects them | a message says adult dependents' claims are private, whether or not any exist.
a 9-year-old with a confidential communication request on file | the subscriber views that dependent | the page looks exactly like one for a dependent with no claims.
a link to the 16-year-old's sensitive-service claim | the subscriber opens it | they see the same "We can't find this claim" page as for a nonexistent claim.
a processed claim | the member selects "Download Explanation of Benefits" | an accessible document opens, with help for other formats or languages.
a claim processed yesterday | the member opens it | it says the EOB is usually ready within 3 business days after processing.
a dependent's hidden claim | the subscriber requests its EOB | the response matches that for a nonexistent claim.
Claim-status calls from portal-registered members fall 25% in the 90 days after launch versus the 90 days before.
In moderated usability testing, 9 of 10 members find a claim's status and next step in under 60 seconds.
No restricted dependent claim is shown to a subscriber in user acceptance testing or the first 90 days (privacy audit sample).
Portal status matches the claims system within 24 hours for 99.5% of sampled claims.
Member-facing pages pass a WCAG 2.2 AA audit before launch.
At least 95% of denied claims show a mapped plain-language reason.
System MUST offer only the 2027 catalog's three standard dental riders, capturing effective date, eligible classes, dependent eligibility and each class's contribution split.

System MUST check at submission that the group is active, the rider fits the base plan, required fields are complete and the effective date is the first of a month at least 30 calendar days after approval (the day it passes these checks).
System MUST send shorter lead times to an exception route needing product owner and underwriting approval with a reason.
System MUST NOT accept a retired rider or a duplicate open request for the same group and rider.
System MUST build the configuration package from catalog values only; non-standard benefits go to the custom-benefit process.
System MUST start deductibles and annual maximums at zero on the rider's effective date, unprorated, and apply the base plan's dependent age limit and new-hire waiting period.
System MUST require a second configuration analyst, never the author, to approve each package and each change.
System MUST re-validate a request when its catalog version changes and hold the package for product owner approval.
System MUST send Fabrikam a synthetic test eligibility file covering every eligible class and record its response.
System MUST alert the vendor manager after 5 business days without a Fabrikam response and count each request's days waiting on the administrator.
System MUST compare expected and actual results for the eight test claims, raise a defect on any mismatch, and re-run all eight after any change.
System MUST block go-live until the package is approved, Fabrikam has accepted the test file and all eight test claims match.
System MUST re-validate a changed effective date as a new request and cancel requests for groups that terminate before go-live.
System MUST show each request's stage, owner, business days in stage and blockers, and flag to the product owner any request in one stage for more than 5 business days.
System MUST hold only group, product and synthetic test data, never real member data; account managers see only their own groups' requests.
System MUST log who did what and when for every change, approval, exception and stage change, kept per the records-retention schedule.

Northwind Traders (GRP-10482) is active on a base plan compatible with Dental Plus | the account manager submits complete request RR-2026-0117 on 2026-11-18, effective 2027-01-01 | it is approved and moves to configuration.
a request missing one class's contribution split and effective mid-month (2027-01-15) | it is submitted | the system names both problems plainly and keeps it in draft.
today is 2026-11-18 | a request effective 2026-12-01 is submitted | it goes to the exception route, needing product owner and underwriting approval with a recorded reason.
Tailspin Toys' base plan is incompatible with Dental Complete | that rider is chosen | the request is blocked with a plain explanation and the compatible riders listed.

approved request RR-2026-0117 for Dental Plus | the analyst generates the package | deductible, annual maximum, preventive, basic and major coinsurance, waiting periods and frequency limits come from the catalog and cannot be typed in.
a rider effective 2027-07-01, midway through the group's plan year | the package is generated | deductibles and annual maximums start at zero that day, with no proration.
a generated package | the analyst who generated it tries to approve it | the system refuses and asks for a second analyst.
the Dental Plus catalog version changed after approval | the package is generated | the request is re-validated, differences are listed and the package waits for product owner approval.
an approved package for GRP-10482 | Fabrikam Dental Administrators accepts a synthetic test eligibility file that includes member CHP-0004417 | the acceptance is recorded as readiness evidence.
Fabrikam rejects the test file | the rejection is recorded | go-live stays blocked and the request returns to configuration with Fabrikam's errors attached.
Fabrikam has not responded within 5 business days | the fifth business day ends | the vendor manager is alerted and the request shows as waiting on the administrator.
Fabrikam has accepted the test file | all eight test claims match expected results in the claims test region | the request is ready to pay claims.
the annual-maximum-reached test claim pays more than expected | the result is recorded | go-live is blocked and a defect with both results returns the request to configuration.
RR-2026-0117 is waiting on Fabrikam | the account manager or product owner opens it | they see its stage, owner, business days in stage and blocker.
a request has been in one stage for more than 5 business days | the sixth business day begins | it is flagged to the product owner.
Median elapsed time from approved request to ready to pay claims falls 40% against the previous 12 months.
At least 90% of requests pass validation on first submission.
Zero pilot go-lives have a benefit mismatch found after the effective date.
Handoffs outside the system (emails, spreadsheets) fall to 2 or fewer per request.
No request is returned for missing or wrong information more than once (clarification loops ≤ 1).
100% of requests show time spent waiting on the administrator.
System MUST give each fax or scanned batch a tracking ID, receipt timestamp (for mail, the mailroom's date-received stamp) and page count.
System MUST split multi-document faxes before classification; a person confirms uncertain splits.
System MUST classify each document as a claim form, medical record, prior-authorization request, appeal or grievance, provider correspondence, or Other, with a confidence score.
System MUST auto-route only non-Other documents at or above their type's threshold; the rest go to human review with a reason.
System MUST let Operations set each type's threshold (0.90 at launch) and record every change.
System MUST pause a type's auto-routing when its misroute rate exceeds 2% over a rolling week and alert the product owner; only a person resumes it.
System MUST extract member ID, name, date of birth, claim number and provider identifiers, with confidence scores.
System MUST attach automatically only on an exact member-ID match plus a matching date of birth or claim number; otherwise a reviewer sees candidate matches.
System MUST hold, unattached, any document whose identifiers point to different members, for privacy-trained reviewers only.
System MUST still attach documents for members whose coverage has ended, flagged "coverage ended".
System MUST pause automatic attachment and open a Privacy Office incident review whenever a wrong-member attachment is found.
System MUST show reviewers only the document, suggestions and member details needed to confirm a match, and let them confirm, correct with a reason code, or escalate.
System MUST keep corrections as labeled examples inside production, used only under Privacy Office procedures; evaluation elsewhere uses only synthetic or de-identified documents.
System MUST start a deadline clock at receipt, including nights, weekends and holidays, for every confirmed or suggested prior-authorization request, appeal or grievance.
System MUST flag expedited documents and put them first; uncertain ones count as expedited until a person decides.
System MUST alert the supervisor when half a window passes unassigned, and the on-call queue when expedited documents arrive outside business hours.
System MUST report the User Story 5 measures daily by type, without member identifiers or document content.
System MUST reconcile every received page daily and report any gap to the intake supervisor.
System MUST audit-log every view, route, attachment and correction, by a person or the system.
System MUST lose nothing during an outage, keep clocks running from receipt, and clear the backlog earliest deadline first.
System MUST process and store documents only in environments approved for protected health information, under the existing records-retention schedule.
System MUST NOT decide any authorization, appeal, grievance or claim; people decide.
claim forms classified at 0.96 and 0.72 against a 0.90 threshold | routing runs | the first reaches the claims queue untouched; the second goes to human review.
fax FAX-20261118-0042 with blank or unreadable pages | it is classified | it goes to human review marked "unreadable".
a fax holding an appeal and a medical record | it arrives | it is split into two documents, and a person confirms any uncertain split.
a document showing member ID CHP-0004417 and that member's claim CLM-2026-000183 | matching runs | the document is attached to both.
an exact member-ID match, a different date of birth and no claim number | matching runs | a reviewer sees candidate matches with only the details needed to confirm one.
a document showing member ID CHP-0004417 and another member's claim | matching runs | the document goes on privacy hold, unattached, for a privacy-trained reviewer.
an exact match for a member whose coverage has ended | matching runs | it is still attached, flagged "coverage ended".

a task suggesting "medical record" at 0.71 | the reviewer changes it to "appeal or grievance" with a reason code | it routes to the appeals and grievances queue, clocked from receipt, and the correction becomes a labeled example.
a reviewer who cannot decide | they escalate | the task moves to the supervisor queue and any clock keeps running.
an expedited prior-authorization request received at 9:05 a.m. | it is routed at 9:20 a.m. | it tops the utilization-management queue, flagged, clocked from 9:05 a.m.
an unassigned expedited appeal | half its window has passed | the queue supervisor is alerted.
an expedited appeal received at 11:40 p.m. on a Saturday | it is classified | its clock starts at 11:40 p.m. and the on-call queue is notified.

yesterday's documents | the intake report opens | it shows by type the volume, auto-route, human-review and misroute rates, time to queue, deadline-risk items and unreconciled pages, without member identifiers.
provider correspondence misrouted at 2.4% over the past week | the rate is calculated | its auto-routing pauses and the product owner is alerted.
Within 60 days of pilot start, at least 60% of documents auto-route untouched, with misroutes at 2% or less.
Median time from receipt to the correct queue falls from today's baseline to 30 minutes or less.
Zero documents attached to the wrong member; any occurrence triggers FR-011.
100% of expedited prior-authorization requests and appeals reach the correct queue within 60 minutes of receipt, at any hour.
Manual keying time per document falls 50% against a time-study baseline.
100% of received pages are reconciled daily.
System MUST capture rider, effective date, eligible employee classes and dependent eligibility for every request.
System MUST accept only first-of-month effective dates at least 30 calendar days after approval, unless the product owner and underwriting approve an exception.
System MUST block requests for groups that are inactive or whose coverage ends before the effective date.
System MUST build configuration from the benefit grid only, with approval by a second configuration analyst.
System MUST start allowances and frequency limits fresh on the rider's effective date, with no proration or carry-over.
System MUST apply the base plan's dependent age limit and new-hire waiting period.
System MUST send Fabrikam Vision Services a synthetic test eligibility file before go-live, record its response, and alert the vendor manager after 5 business days without one.
System MUST compare expected and actual results for the eight standard test claims and return any mismatch to configuration.
System MUST block go-live until configuration is approved, Fabrikam has accepted the test file and all eight test claims match.
System MUST cancel a request when its group terminates before go-live and tell Fabrikam to drop the group.
System MUST log who approved what and when, and use only synthetic members, such as CHP-0002286, in tests.
Woodgrove Bank (GRP-20417) is active on a compatible base plan | complete request RR-2025-0042 is submitted on 2025-05-12, effective 2025-07-01 | it is approved and moves to configuration.
today is 2025-06-10 | a request effective 2025-07-01 is submitted | it needs product owner and underwriting approval with a recorded reason.
Alpine Ski House's coverage ends before the requested effective date | a request is submitted | it is blocked with a plain explanation.
approved request RR-2025-0042 | the configuration analyst builds the package | copays, frame and contact lens allowances and frequency limits match the benefit grid.
a built package | the analyst who built it tries to approve it | approval is refused until a second analyst reviews it.
a rider effective 2025-07-01 for a group with a January plan year | the package is built | allowances and frequency limits start fresh that day, with no proration.
an approved package | Fabrikam accepts a synthetic test file with an employee, a dependent child and a new hire | the acceptance is recorded as readiness evidence.
Fabrikam rejects the file or is silent for 5 business days | that is recorded | go-live stays blocked and the vendor manager is alerted.

Fabrikam has accepted the test file | the eight standard test claims run (exam, lenses, frames, contacts instead of glasses, frequency limit reached, out-of-network, dependent child, terminated member) | all match expected results.
the frames claim pays above the allowance | the result is recorded | go-live is blocked and the request returns to configuration with the evidence.
every readiness check has passed | the effective date arrives | the rider is active for eligible employees and dependents.
an employee in a new-hire waiting period | the rider goes live | their rider starts when their medical coverage starts.
the group terminates before go-live | that is recorded | the request is cancelled and Fabrikam is told to drop the group.
Fabrikam accepts every group's test eligibility file before the group's effective date.
Zero benefit mismatches are found after any group's effective date.
At least 90% of requests pass validation on first submission.
No rider starts inside the 30-day lead time without a recorded exception approval.
